a: The ID to use for the acl, which will become the final component of the acl's name. The structure of 'aclId' defines the Resource Pattern (resource_type, resource_name, pattern_type) of the acl.
ID of the location of the Kafka resource. See https://cloud.google.com/managed-kafka/docs/locations for a list of supported locations.
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
The operation type. Allowed values are (case insensitive): ALL, READ, WRITE, CREATE, DELETE, ALTER, DESCRIBE, CLUSTER_ACTION, DESCRIBE_CONFIGS, ALTER_CONFIGS, and IDEMPOTENT_WRITE.
The principal. Specified as Google Cloud account, with the Kafka StandardAuthorizer prefix User:". For example: "User:test-kafka-client@test-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com".
The host. Must be set to "*" for Managed Service for Apache Kafka.
The permission type. Accepted values are (case insensitive): ALLOW, DENY.

The ID to use for the cluster, which will become the final component of the cluster's name. The ID must be 1-63 characters long, and match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' to comply with RFC 1035.
ID of the location of the Kafka resource. See https://cloud.google.com/managed-kafka/docs/locations for a list of supported locations.
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
List of label KEY=VALUE pairs to add. Keys must start with a lowercase character and contain only hyphens (-), underscores ( ), lowercase characters, and numbers.
The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
The memory to provision for the cluster in bytes. The value must be between 1 GiB and 8 GiB per vCPU. Ex. 1024Mi, 4Gi.
The number of vCPUs to provision for the cluster. The minimum is 3.
The Cloud KMS Key name to use for encryption. The key must be located in the same region as the cluster and cannot be changed.
Name of the VPC subnet from which the cluster is accessible. Both broker and bootstrap server IP addresses and DNS entries are automatically created in the subnet.

A list of IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges that are allowed to connect to the cluster. To protect your cluster, allow access from only trusted external IP ranges. Don't expose your cluster to untrusted ranges.
The disk to provision for each broker in Gibibytes. Minimum: 100 GiB.
The rebalance behavior for the cluster. When not specified, defaults to 'NO_REBALANCE'. Possible values: 'MODE_UNSPECIFIED', 'NO_REBALANCE', 'AUTO_REBALANCE_ON_SCALE_UP'.
The rules for mapping mTLS certificate Distinguished Names (DNs) to shortened principal names for Kafka ACLs.
The name of the CA pool to pull CA certificates from. The CA pool does not need to be in the same project or location as the Kafka cluster.
The ID to use for the Connect Cluster, which will become the final component of the connect cluster's name. This value is structured like: 'my-connect-cluster-id'.
The name of the Kafka cluster this Kafka Connect cluster is attached to. Structured like: 'projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/clusters/CLUSTER_ID'.
ID of the location of the Kafka Connect resource. See https://cloud.google.com/managed-kafka/docs/locations for a list of supported locations.
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
List of label KEY=VALUE pairs to add. Keys must start with a lowercase character and contain only hyphens (-), underscores ( ), lowercase characters, and numbers.
The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
The memory to provision for the cluster in bytes. The CPU:memory ratio (vCPU:GiB) must be between 1:1 and 1:8. Minimum: 3221225472 (3 GiB).
The number of vCPUs to provision for the cluster. The minimum is 3.
VPC subnet to make available to the Kafka Connect cluster. Structured like: projects/{project}/regions/{region}/subnetworks/{subnet_id}.
Additional DNS domain names from the subnet's network to be made visible to the Connect Cluster.
The ID to use for the connector, which will become the final component of the connector's name. This value is structured like: 'my-connector-id'.
ID of the location of the Kafka Connect resource. See https://cloud.google.com/managed-kafka/docs/locations for a list of supported locations.
Connector config as keys/values. The keys of the map are connector property names, for example: 'connector.class', 'tasks.max', 'key.converter'.
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

The maximum amount of time to wait before retrying a failed task. This sets an upper bound for the backoff delay. A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".

The minimum amount of time to wait before retrying a failed task. This sets a lower bound for the backoff delay. A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".
ID of the location of the Kafka resource. See https://cloud.google.com/managed-kafka/docs/locations for a list of supported locations.
The number of replicas of each partition. A replication factor of 3 is recommended for high availability.
The ID to use for the topic, which will become the final component of the topic's name. This value is structured like: 'my-topic-name'.
Configuration for the topic that are overridden from the cluster defaults. The key of the map is a Kafka topic property name, for example: 'cleanup.policy=compact', 'compression.type=producer'.
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".

The number of partitions in a topic. You can increase the partition count for a topic, but you cannot decrease it. Increasing partitions for a topic that uses a key might change how messages are distributed.
The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
